absent: Numeric values of feature bits, ioctl commands, error codes, and file mode flags beyond their names.
Internals of range validation, atomic page fill, page move, protection application, and fault wake helpers referenced but not routed.
Full structure definitions, field offsets, and sizes for context, wake range, and control request types.
Locking, lifetime, and concurrency rules for bucket allocator, slab cache, sysctl state, and virtual area file handling beyond shown calls.
Fault delivery, polling, and read path behavior that consumes queued faults and events.
Architecture specific page table support predicates and compatibility task detection details.

findings.text: The dossier exposes creation of a userfaultfd object through a system call taking flags and through a device operation taking flags. Creation validates flags against a shared set plus a user mode only bit, checks permission for kernel fault handling via privilege or a sysctl controlled allowance for unprivileged callers, allocates a context, pins the caller address space, and publishes an anonymous file with nonblocking behavior.

Once created, the file supports a multiplexed control operation that requires prior feature negotiation for every command except the negotiation itself. The dispatcher routes registration, unregistration, wake, copy, zero page, move, write protection, continue, poison, read write protection, and mode setting to dedicated handlers and rejects unknown commands.

The file declares operations for release, polling, iterated reads, control, compatibility control, and a no operation seek, with an optional file descriptor info hook. The info hook reports counts of pending and total fault queue entries and the negotiated protocol identity, feature set, and control set.
Initialization registers a misc device for on demand creation, creates a slab cache for contexts with queue initialization, and registers sysctl controls for unprivileged and virtual memory behavior.

Handlers for protection, continue, poison, and move share a validation contract. They refuse work while the address space is changing, validate the supplied range against the bound address space, reject unknown mode bits, require the bound address space to remain alive during the operation, and translate lifetime loss into a missing process style error.

Feature negotiation checks protocol version, requires privilege for fork event tracking, expands asynchronous write protection tracking to include unpopulated tracking, requires base read write protection for its asynchronous variant, reports the full available feature and control sets, refuses any requested bit outside availability, publishes the negotiated set back to the caller, and allows exactly one successful initialization per context with failure clearing the returned description.

The available feature set starts from a build time collection and is reduced when architecture minor fault support is absent, when page table support for user fault write tracking is absent, when write protection marker support is absent, and when read write protection support is unavailable either at compile time or at runtime.

Move additionally forbids cross address space operation by requiring the bound space to be the caller space, validates both source and destination ranges independently for the same length, and accepts only hole tolerance and no wake modifiers.

Address randomization helpers apply only under explicit opt in or architecture defaults. Stack top randomization offsets by a masked random page count in a direction dependent on growth, page randomization aligns and clamps then adds a random page offset, break randomization uses a smaller window for compatibility tasks and a larger window otherwise, and mmap randomization draws from a bit width that may differ for compatibility tasks.

Locked memory accounting requires address space write exclusion, enforces the caller memory lock limit unless bypassed, increments the locked total only on success, decrements on release with a warning if underflow would occur, and emits a debug record identifying caller, direction, sizes, limits, and limit exceedance.

Mode setting evolves context features after initialization. It accepts disjoint enable and disable sets limited to toggleable and actually supported bits, requires base read write protection before its asynchronous form, drains in flight faults across armed regions under write exclusion, publishes the new feature set once, and when entering asynchronous mode wakes all waiters so blocked faults retry under the new behavior.

Continue, poison, and move report progress as a byte count written back to the caller structure. A fully completed range returns success while a short completion asks the caller to retry, a no wake request suppresses the completion wake, and otherwise completion wakes waiters interested in the affected range with the destination range used for move.

Mmap base selection chooses between legacy bottom up placement and top down placement. Legacy applies for compatibility layout personality, unlimited stack on downward growth systems, or a sysctl default. Top down reserves a gap derived from the stack limit plus guard and randomization pad, clamped between minimum and maximum bounds, then subtracts randomization. A fallback configuration always selects bottom up at a fixed base.

Feature mutation serializes against fault handling by holding address space write exclusion while waiting for per region readers on every armed region to drain, then publishing the feature word with a single atomic store so lockless observers never see a partial update, with hot path readers already ordered by the drain.

Fault queue inspection and asynchronous wake up serialize on the pending queue spin lock with interrupts disabled. The info path counts both pending and general queue membership under this lock, while mode transition wakes both queues under the same lock.

The context object carries a reference count, creation flags, a feature word starting clear, a released marker, a changing lock, a changing counter, a bound address space pointer, multiple wait queues for pending faults, faults, events, and file wakeup, plus a refile sequence tied to the pending queue lock. Slab initialization prepares the wait queues and sequence, while creation initializes counts, locks, and the address space pin.

File behavior is described by two operation tables and a misc device descriptor. The main table binds release, poll, iterated read, control, compatibility control, and seek with conditional info support. The device table binds control, compatibility control, ownership, and seek. The device descriptor names the device and requests dynamic minor allocation, registered at init alongside slab and sysctl setup.

The memory utility area provides allocation with duplication for bounded strings and raw buffers. String helpers guarantee termination, return null on null input or allocation failure, share a common bounded copy core, avoid duplication when the input already resides in read only kernel data, and scale element counts safely before copying. Raw helpers copy exact lengths with node aware or virtual allocation variants.

User memory duplication helpers allocate from a dedicated bucket pool created at init and copy from user space. One variant uses virtual allocation while the other uses tracked bucket allocation with extra space for termination. Allocation failure yields an out of memory error pointer and copy failure frees the buffer and yields a bad address error pointer.

Two virtual area helpers are provided. One tests whether the current stack pointer lies within a given area to identify the current stack. The other replaces the file backing of a non anonymous area while maintaining reference counts on old and new files.

The address space layout and accounting area exposes stack top and page randomization, break and mmap randomization, legacy detection, top down base computation, layout selection, and locked memory charging. Callers supply stack limits and page counts and receive randomized addresses, layout side effects on the address space descriptor, and limit enforcement results.

Completion handling treats zero progress as a broadcast wake rather than a ranged wake and warns on unexpected zero progress, so callers must handle spurious wakes. Short completions are not errors but retry signals. Operations racing address space changes or teardown fail rather than block, and protection changes can optionally suppress wakes leaving waiters pending.

Duplication paths must handle null input, allocation failure, user copy failure, length overflow on termination space, and range overflow in page randomization. Failures return null or typed error pointers and, for user copies, release any partial allocation before returning.

The toggleable feature mask fact is that only the asynchronous read write protection bit may change after initialization. This mask gates mode setting enable and disable validation in combination with runtime availability.

Layout bound facts are a minimum gap of one hundred twenty eight megabytes, a maximum gap of five sixths of the stack top, and a stack randomization mask covering eight megabytes of virtual address expressed as a page shifted value.

The control surface fact is that distinct ABI identifiers exist for protocol version negotiation, fork, minor, write protection, and read write protection features, and for register, wake, copy, zero page, move, write protect, continue, poison, read write protect, and mode control operations.
